stem:
The structure of the polydentate ligand, $\text{EDTA}^{4-}$, is shown in Fig. 4.1.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 4.1

The stability constants, at $298\text{ K}$, of five octahedral complexes are given in Table 4.1.

Table 4.1

| complex | $K_{\text{stab}}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $[\text{Cu(EDTA)}]^{2-}$ | $6.31 \times 10^{19}$ |
| $[\text{Cr(EDTA)}]^{2-}$ | $1.00 \times 10^{13}$ |
| $[\text{Cr(EDTA)}]^{-}$ | $1.00 \times 10^{24}$ |
| $[\text{Fe(EDTA)}]^{2-}$ | $2.00 \times 10^{14}$ |
| $[\text{Fe(EDTA)}]^{-}$ | $1.26 \times 10^{25}$ |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the oxidation states of Cu in $[\text{Cu(EDTA)}]^{2-}$ and Cr in $[\text{Cr(EDTA)}]^{-}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Deduce the number of lone pairs donated by each $\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ ligand in a single $[\text{Fe(EDTA)}]^{2-}$ complex ion.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Identify the most stable complex in Table 4.1. Explain your choice.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
In a solution at equilibrium at $298\text{ K}$, $[[\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}] = 3.00 \times 10^{-10}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ and $[\text{EDTA}^{4-}] = 5.00 \times 10^{-12}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

Use the expression for $K_{\text{stab}}$ to calculate the concentration of $[\text{Cu(EDTA)}]^{2-}$ in this solution.

Show your working.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
A solution of $[\text{Cu(EDTA)}]^{2-}$ ions is pale blue while a solution of $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]^{2+}$ ions is deep blue.

Explain this difference in colour.
